info.description:
Enterprise-grade API for high-value gear rentals. Build your own adventure apps powered by the Splitt network.

**Global prefix:** every route is served under `/api/v1`.

**Authentication:** protected routes require a `Bearer <JWT>` Authorization header (obtain a token from `POST /api/v1/users/login`).

**Money fields:** monetary amounts are serialized as decimal **strings** (e.g. `"195.00"`), never JS numbers — parse with care to avoid float drift.

**Errors:** every error response uses the standard `ApiErrorResponse` envelope (`statusCode`, `error`, `message`, `requestId`, ...).

SPLIT-411 / SPLIT-317: PATCH /admin/users/:id/access
Atomically set BOTH a user's base persona and entitlement set in one DB

whitelisted to their enums (bad value → 400), missing user → 404. Replaces
the Access Control Center's previous two sequential PATCHes (role then

SPLIT-671: web Sign in with Apple — initiation leg. Mirrors
`GET /auth/google`: issue the one-time CSRF state (with its derived nonce)
and bounce the browser to Apple's authorize page.

post.summary:
SPLIT-285: native Sign in with Apple. The client posts Apple's
`identityToken`; Apple only sends the user's name on the first authorization
(and only to the client), so `firstName`/`lastName` ride along on that first
call and are used only when provisioning a brand-new account.

SPLIT-671: web Sign in with Apple — return leg. Because scopes are
requested, Apple answers with `response_mode=form_post`: an HTTP POST of
urlencoded fields (`code`, `id_token`, `state`, first-auth-only `user`
JSON, or `error=user_cancelled_authorize`) — a top-level cross-site POST,
which is exactly why the CSRF gate is the server-side one-time `state`
row (cookies would need SameSite=None here). Like the Google GET
callback, fields are validated by hand and every failure answers with a
REDIRECT — this is browser navigation, not a JSON API.

The id_token is verified locally (RS256 vs Apple JWKS + iss/aud/exp +
SPLIT-427 verified-email) with one web-only addition: its `nonce` claim
must echo sha256(state), binding the token to the flow WE initiated.

get.summary:
SPLIT-649: Google redirects the BROWSER here with `?code=…&state=…` — a
GET (this was wrongly `@Post`, so the real flow 404'd and never worked).
Query params are validated by hand (not a strict DTO): Google appends
extra params (`scope`, `authuser`, `prompt`, …) that the global
`forbidNonWhitelisted` pipe would 400, and a top-level browser navigation
must answer errors with a REDIRECT, not a JSON error body.

On success the user is redirected to the frontend with a short-lived
one-time code — `POST /auth/oauth/exchange` swaps it for the session.
The JWT itself never rides in a URL any more (it leaked via history,
proxies and Referer headers).

post.summary:
SPLIT-649: swap the one-time code from the callback redirect for the real
session. Returns EXACTLY the `POST /users/login` envelope (access token,
refresh token, compact user) via the same `authService.login` path — so
web social auth gains refresh-token support and the suspension check.
Unknown, replayed or expired codes are all the same opaque 401.

SPLIT-628: thin delegate. The verify → dedup → dispatch → record flow (a
verbatim copy of the payments webhook, plus an outer catch-all that masked
even transient DB errors as 400 "Invalid webhook") now lives in
StripeConnectService.handleConnectWebhook on the SHARED pipeline. New
semantics: missing/invalid signature or unset secret → 400 WITH the
reason; processing failure → 500 (Stripe retries); duplicate → 200 no-op.
@SkipThrottle: Stripe delivery bursts must never 429 — the signature
verification inside the pipeline is the gate (the anonymous-IP ceiling in
GlobalAnonThrottleGuard skips this path too).
